question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: WHITESPACE is the WS set only. Any run of it may stand before or after any token — between a composite's name and its "[" too ("list [text]" and "list\n[text]" parse) — and at either end of the text, and is ignored there. It may not stand inside a name. Every other character outside a name or a token — a no-break space, a form feed, a vertical tab, any non-ASCII character — is not whitespace and makes the text throw.
The text is one TYPE (R3) and nothing after it but whitespace; leftover text throws ("text none", "list[text] x").

TYPE = an ALT, then zero or more of: "|" followed by an ALT. Two or more alts make a union whose alts are the nodes in written order, nothing reordered. A single alt is its own node. Every "|" must be followed by an alt ("text |", "text || none" and "| text" throw). An alt is never itself a union node: a union inside a union exists only as a part of a composite.

UNREACHABLE ALTERNATIVE: a union throws when some alt is COVERED (R6) by an alt written EARLIER in the same union, adjacent or not. Order matters: "text | json" and "none | json" parse; "json | text", "json | none" and "json | json" throw. The rule holds at every level ("list[i64 | i64]" and "list[json | f64]" throw), and is checked once all of that union's alts are read.

SAME TYPE: two nodes are the same type when their k is equal and — tuple: the same count of items, pairwise the same type in written order; list: the items the same type; map: keys the same type and vals the same type; record: the same set of field names, each name's two types the same, field ORDER ignored; union: the same set of alts up to the same type, alt ORDER ignored; a scalar: nothing more. Whitespace never matters. So "list[text | none] | list[none | text]" and "record[a: text, b: i64] | record[b: i64, a: text]" throw, while "tuple[text, i64] | tuple[i64, text]", "record[a: text] | record[b: text]" and "record[a: text, b: i64] | record[b: text, a: i64]" parse.

COVERS: an earlier alt E covers a later alt L exactly when one of these holds, applied recursively to the parts: (a) E and L are the same type (R5); (b) E is json and L is JSON-SHAPED: none, bool, f64, text or json; a list whose item is JSON-SHAPED; a tuple every item of which is; a map whose key is exactly the scalar text and whose val is; a record every field type of which is; a union every alt of which is; (c) both are lists and E's item covers L's item; (d) both are tuples of the same item count and each item of E covers L's item at the same position; (e) both are maps, E's key covers L's key and E's val covers L's val; (f) both are records and every field of E has a field of the same name in L that E's field type covers — L may have MORE fields than E, never fewer ("record[a: text] | record[a: text, b: none]" throws, the reverse order parses); (g) E is a union and some alt of E covers L; (h) L is a union and E covers every alt of L. (g) and (h) arise only on parts, since an alt is never a union. Nothing else covers: bytes, i64 and u64 are never JSON-SHAPED; a map keyed by anything but the bare scalar text is not ("json | map[text | none, json]" parses); no form covers another form ("list[text] | tuple[text]", "map[text, text] | record[a: text]" and "f64 | i64" parse); and coverage is by ONE earlier alt, never by several jointly ("tuple[text] | tuple[none] | tuple[text | none]" parses).

ALT begins with a NAME, the longest run of IDENT characters there (the IDENT pin). A NAME equal to a scalar of TABLE NODE -> that scalar node. A NAME equal to tuple, list, map or record must be followed (after optional whitespace) by "[" and continues as R8 or R9. Every other NAME throws (case-sensitive: "Text", "text2", "textnone", "option" throw).

COMPOSITE: inside the brackets, one or more TYPEs (R3, so a part may be a union) separated by ",", then "]". No empty part and no trailing comma. tuple takes any count of one or more as its items; list takes exactly one as its item; map takes exactly two, key then val. Any other count throws ("tuple[]", "list[text, i64]", "map[text]").

RECORD: inside the brackets, one or more FIELDs separated by ",", then "]". FIELD = a name matching the IDENT pin, ":", a TYPE (R3). Field names are unique within one record, compared exactly (case-sensitive: "A" and "a" differ); a repeated name throws. A field name may equal a type name ("record[text: text]"). Fields keep written order.

NESTING CAP: composites (tuple, list, map, record) nest at most MAX_DEPTH deep. The depth of a composite is the count of composites enclosing it plus one; siblings do not add up ("tuple[list[i64], list[i64]]" is depth 2). A text whose composites reach depth MAX_DEPTH parses; one that reaches MAX_DEPTH + 1 throws — however deep it goes, it throws and never exhausts the host. Scalars and unions add no type depth, but they do add RESULT depth: counting the root node as level 0 and each member value, list element and field pair one deeper, a record-of-union chain costs 5 levels per composite, the most of any form, so the deepest legal result is 5 × MAX_DEPTH + 3 levels — inside MAX_VALUE_DEPTH.

Brackets therefore always balance: a missing "]", an extra "]" or a stray "[" leaves R2–R9 unsatisfied and throws. Every violation of R1–R10 throws, wherever it sits in the nesting; the message is not graded.
scalar | k = one of text, bytes, bool, none, i64, u64, f64, json
union  | k = "union"; alts = list of nodes, at least two, no alt covered by an earlier one (R4), never a union node
tuple  | k = "tuple"; items = list of nodes, at least one
map    | k = "map"; key = a node; val = a node
record | k = "record"; fields = list of two-element lists [name text, node], at least one, in written order
MAX_VALUE_DEPTH | 100 (the value codec's nesting cap; above 5 × MAX_DEPTH + 3, so it never bounds the oracle)
